Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleVista Communications Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, you will need to press star one on your telephone. If you require operator assistance at any time, please press star zero. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleVista Communications' Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Kim, Chief Network Officer; Lisa Torres, Chief Commercial Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Mike Harlan, Chief Operating Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong second quarter, demonstrating our continued commitment to growth and innovation. Our success is driven by our dedicated team and strategic investments.

Our key achievements include favorable subscriber acquisition cost trends, with blended SAC at $428 per net new subscriber, down 8% year-over-year. We're making solid progress on operating expense management, delivering $285 million in year-over-year savings that boosted profitability. Our spectrum assets are seeing improved utilization at 72% network-wide, with clear plans for future allocation through refarming and auctions. Cost of revenue trends show efficiencies despite growth, with gross margins expanding. ARPU is trending up 3.6% year-over-year to $55.75, thanks to pricing and bundling. New product launches like 5G Ultra FWA generated $285 million in incremental revenue and 1.2 million net adds. Service revenues grew 6.2% across wireless, broadband, and enterprise. Finally, fiber buildout advanced with 7.8 million homes passed and 2.4 million subscribers.

The launch of 5G Ultra FWA is exceeding expectations, resulting in 750,000 net adds and $142 million in revenue. Further milestones are strong service revenue growth in broadband at 8.5% YoY. We are also focusing on ARPU uplift from bundles. Our dedication to spectrum optimization is bearing fruit. Our strategy is to enhance fiber adoption with 31% take rates. We are actively investing in new services like NexStream+. We are also exploring edge AI for enterprise and finally, analyzing OpEx initiatives for margin expansion.

Maria Chen: Thank you, Alex. Now, let's review our financial performance. Revenue for the quarter reached $18.2 billion, reflecting a 5.8% increase year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was $6.95 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.2%. We maintain a disciplined approach to cost management and capital allocation. Capital expenditures totaled $2.8 billion, primarily allocated to expanding our 5G network, fiber infrastructure, and content investments.

I'll now turn to our subscriber acquisition cost trends, which remain a key focus area as we navigate a highly competitive telecommunications and media landscape. Our discussion today includes forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act. Actual results may differ materially due to factors outlined in our SEC filings.

In Q2 2024, our blended SAC came in at $428 per net new subscriber, a modest 2% increase quarter-over-quarter from $420 in Q1, but down 8% year-over-year from $465 in Q2 2023. This reflects the ongoing maturation of our customer acquisition engine amid intensifying competition from T-Mobile's Go5G plans, Verizon's myPlan bundles, and streaming pure-plays like Netflix and Disney+ aggressively targeting broadband and mobility customers. Postpaid wireless SAC was $512, flat QoQ but down 10% YoY, while broadband SAC improved to $285, a 5% QoQ decline driven by organic referrals and upselling within our existing 5G Home footprint.

SAC encompasses direct marketing spend—including digital programmatic ads on platforms like Google DV360 and The Trade Desk—sales commissions to our 15,000 retail partners, device subsidies primarily for iPhone 15/16 series and Galaxy S24 flagships, and onboarding costs like credit checks and SIM provisioning. Excluding one-time 5G spectrum auction amortization, our core SAC would have been $415, underscoring the efficiency gains we're embedding.

The 8% YoY decline is our best in three years, fueled by a 22% ramp in self-serve digital sign-ups via our StreamTel app, now accounting for 35% of mobility adds—up from 22% a year ago. This leverages machine learning algorithms from our partnership with Adobe Experience Cloud to hyper-target cord-cutters with personalized bundles like 5G Unlimited + Disney Bundle + Paramount+, delivering a 15% higher conversion rate at 25% lower cost per lead than traditional TV spots.

The slight 2% QoQ uptick was due to seasonal back-to-school promotions, subsidizing $250 average on mid-tier Android devices for family plans. However, our LTV-to-SAC ratio improved to 3.8x from 3.5x QoQ, as new subs exhibit 12% higher ARPU at $58.20 postpaid wireless thanks to embedded media upsells—our TeleMedia Fusion package now penetrates 42% of new mobility adds, blending 100Mbps fiber with ad-supported tiers from Peacock and Max.

Regionally, North America (78% of adds) saw $445 SAC, up 4% YoY due to price wars in mature markets like the Northeast Corridor, while Sunbelt expansions in Texas and Florida dropped SAC 12% to $390 via door-to-door fiber teams partnering with local MSOs like Cox. Europe (15% of adds) had $365 SAC, down 15% YoY from EU roaming regulations and our Vodafone JV in Germany/Italy, where shared 5G infrastructure cut capex pass-throughs by 18%, aided by UK gains versus BT Openreach. Latin America/APAC (7% of adds) achieved $310 SAC, driven by prepaid-to-postpaid migrations in Brazil via Claro integration and Android-heavy subsidies in India against Jio's dominance, with Starlink backhaul trials yielding 20% cheaper rural acquires.

Our AI-powered Customer Data Platform on Snowflake with Cortex AI has reduced wasteful ad spend by 28% through predictive propensity modeling at 92% accuracy. Edge computing via AWS Outposts at 200 retail locations enables instant eSIM activations, slashing fulfillment by $12 per sub. Zero-rating Paramount+ and Tubi in 5G plans boosts trial-to-paid by 18%, amortizing SAC over longer tenures averaging 28 months versus 24 last year.

Viewed holistically with churn at 1.1% monthly—lowest among the Big 3—SAC payback is under 9 months. We're doubling down on acquire-to-retain with loyalty loops: 3 months free StreamTel+ SVOD hub drives 65% retention at month 12. As we roll out 6GHz Wi-Fi 7 CPE and Open RAN 5G standalone, we expect 10-15% broadband net adds from 5G Home upgrades without extra marketing.

For Q3, we guide SAC to $415-$425, a 3-5% YoY decline, with full-year 2024 at $430, a 7% improvement supporting raised FY24 EBITDA guidance of $18.5B-$19B.

Next, our operating expense management initiatives continue as a cornerstone of profitability. Total OpEx was $4.2 billion, down 6.3% or $285 million YoY, marking three straight quarters of declines amid inflation and AI data center energy costs. Ex-restructuring, core OpEx as % of revenue improved to 62% from 68%. This stems from our VistaLean program, generating $750 million annualized run-rate savings.

Network operations and maintenance yielded $128 million savings (45% of total). We've virtualized 65% of 4G LTE RAN to cloud-native Open RAN with Ericsson and Nokia, reducing site leases 12% via co-location and field maintenance 18% with NetGuard AI. In fixed broadband, decommissioning 15,000 miles of copper shifted customers to XGS-PON fiber, shaving $45 million off depreciation-add-back while boosting fiber penetration to 42% of 25 million broadband subs.

Content costs saved $72 million (25% of total). With SVOD churn at 1.2%, we renegotiated NBCUniversal and Warner Bros. Discovery deals for 8-10% linear carriage discounts across 18 million pay-TV households. FAST channels now 22% of TeleVista Stream viewing, capping original spend at $450 million for the half despite three new series. In Europe as VivaTel, we saved €35 million ($38 million) bundling sports with DAZN and AI-dubbed localization, cutting opex 22%.

SG&A efficiencies of $65 million came from 4,200 headcount reduction (7% non-network), zero-based marketing dropping broadband CAC to $320 from $375 using first-party data from 50 million mobile users, and vendor consolidation from 250 to 180 suppliers for 11% pricing relief.

Regionally, North America (72% revenue) saved $195 million from 5G Ultra Wideband covering 280 million POPS; APAC via 28% IndiWave stake saved $45 million with Jio-like efficiencies; Europe $28 million despite labor costs, aided by Nokia edge partnerships.

These $210 million EBITDA tailwinds after transitional costs funded a 50 bps leverage cut to 2.6x and 15% dividend hike. We see $300-350 million FY run-rate savings, with 5G SA enabling 25% core transport reductions.

Turning to spectrum assets, we hold 245 MHz average licensed across top 100 markets: 40 MHz low-band 600 MHz C-Block, 140 MHz mid-band (100 MHz CBRS 3.45-3.55 GHz, 80 MHz C-band), and 1.8 GHz mmWave in 35 metros. Utilization is 72%, up from 58% two years ago.

Low-band at 82% anchors FWA for 2.8 million households (150% YoY), exceeding 90% in Midwest/Southeast for $450 million EBITDA. Mid-band 75% uses DSS on 85% macros for 1.2 Gbps speeds. mmWave 55% yields $250 ARPU in enterprises. Top 25 markets 81%, secondary 68%; bits/Hz at 12.5.

Future plans: $4.8 billion of $12 billion capex FY24-26 for optimization. Refarming 30 MHz PCS/AWS-3 to 5G NR by Q2 2025 boosts capacity 25%. Budget $1.5 billion for Auction 108 CBRS PALs, $800 million secondary mmWave from DISH-like deals. Slicing 50% mid-band by 2026: 20% media URLLC, 15% FWA, 10% private nets with Open RAN. Piloting RedCap IoT, AI orchestration for 20% uplift, FMC with 25 MHz C-band for 10 million FWA subs.

This delivers 15-20% wireless EBITDA CAGR to 2028, ROIC >12%.

On cost of revenue, it was $5.82 billion, up 7.2% YoY from $5.43 billion but flat QoQ, driving gross margin to 42.1% (+110 bps). Breakdown: network ops $2.62B (+12%/$280M), content $1.745B (+6%/$95M), premises/interconnect $980M (+4%/$40M), spectrum/roaming $280M (-5%/$15M), other $175M (+6%/$10M).

YoY increase volume-driven from 18% traffic/5G, offset by efficiencies: cost/GB $0.058 (-8%) via Open RAN. Content moderated with $120M bundling savings, 40% in-house originals. Premises from 2.5M adds, mitigated by IXP. Spectrum down from eSIM.

QoQ flat despite 5% traffic: cash opex/site $2,800 (-4%) via NFV/SDN, energy +2% contained by renewables/AI shaping.

North America $4.36B (+8%), Europe $875M (+5%), APAC/LatAm $585M (+4%). Q4 guide $5.9-6.0B, +50-80 bps margin.

ARPU trends show postpaid mobile up 4.1% YoY to $52.30 from pricing 3-5% on premium and 60% from bundles like 5G Home + Mobile MegaBundle ($4.20 lift, 42% NA pen). Broadband +2.8% to $72.15 from 7% gigabit hikes, FiberFusion $5.80. Media +5.5% to $15.20 from family plans, All-Access $2.50. Consolidated +3.6% to $55.75. Q4 +3.8-4.2%, FY $56.10, $1.2B revenue add.

New launches: $285M incremental revenue (+175% YoY), 1.2M net adds. 5G Ultra FWA $142M, 750K adds ($78 ARPU). NexStream+ $98M, 320K adds. EdgeAI $45M, 130K connections.

Service revenue $14.8B (+6.2% YoY): wireless $9.2B (+4.2%), broadband $3.1B (+8.5%), enterprise $2.5B (+6.1%).

Fiber: 7.8M homes passed (+28% YoY, 1.2M Q2), 2.4M subs (+37% YoY, 420K QoQ), 31% take rate. Sunbelt 2.9M passed, Midwest 1.8M, etc. YE 9.5M passed.

David Kim: Thank you. I'm pleased to provide an update on our network advancements. We've significantly expanded our 5G coverage, delivering faster speeds and lower latency. Our network reliability remains high, and we are continuously optimizing our infrastructure to meet growing demand. We are also focusing on enhancing our cybersecurity posture. We are committed to pushing spectrum utilization higher through refarming and slicing while accelerating fiber overlays for convergence.

Lisa Torres: Thank you. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We've seen strong subscriber growth across our various service offerings. Customer satisfaction remains a top priority, and we are continuously improving the customer experience. We are also focused on expanding our partnerships to offer bundled services and enhance customer value. We are prioritizing ARPU expansion via targeted pricing and sticky bundles like TeleMedia Fusion, alongside SAC efficiencies from digital self-serve.

Raj Patel: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to transform our business. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations, improve customer service, and develop new products and services. We are also investing in research and development to stay ahead of the curve. Our technological direction is toward Open RAN, edge AI, and 5G SA for dynamic allocation and low-latency media delivery.

Mike Harlan: Thank you. Operationally, we are focused on improving efficiency and streamlining our processes. We are leveraging data analytics to optimize our resource allocation and improve decision-making. We are also committed to sustainability and reducing our environmental impact. Our operational focus is VistaLean OpEx controls, virtualization, and decommissioning legacy assets to fund growth.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your content strategy and your plans for investing in original programming, and what is the anticipated impact on subscriber growth?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, John. Our content strategy emphasizes convergence, blending telecom with media through bundles like NexStream+ and TeleMedia Fusion, which include FAST channels, sports rights, and AI-personalized originals. We've capped spend at $450 million for the half while launching three unscripted series and shifting 40% to in-house via AI workflows, saving costs. Renegotiated deals with NBCU and WBD yield discounts, and zero-rated streaming boosts trials. This drove 320,000 NexStream+ adds and 15% vMVPD share, with media ARPU +5.5% to $15.20. We expect originals to add 500,000-700,000 subs in H2, lifting blended growth 2-3 points via 65% bundle attachment.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for addressing the digital divide and ensuring that all communities have access to affordable broadband, and how do you plan to achieve 10 million FWA subscribers by 2027?

Lisa Torres: Great question, Emily. We're tackling the digital divide head-on with 5G FWA and fiber. FWA serves 2.8 million households already, targeting 30 million DSL/cable homes with gigabit speeds under 20ms latency using low/mid-band spectrum. Fiber passed 7.8 million homes, with RDOF/BEAD subsidies for rural—$450 million application for 500,000 passings. Sunbelt/Midwest builds add 800K-900K quarterly. Affordable bundles like FiberFusion at $78 ARPU include media, driving 31% take rates and 52% in greenfields. For 10M FWA, we're allocating 25 MHz C-band, hybrid backhaul, and partnerships, expecting 4-5M FY24 adds total broadband.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez: Can you discuss your capital allocation priorities and your plans for returning capital to shareholders, including dividend growth and buybacks?

Maria Chen: Thanks, Mike. Priorities remain growth capex at $2.8B quarterly for 5G/fiber, then debt reduction—leverage to 2.6x—followed by returns. OpEx savings $285M and EBITDA torque fund 15% dividend hike this quarter. Buybacks: $1.5B authorized remaining, targeting 2-3% FCF yield expansion. Post-5G build, FCF inflects 2025 for more shareholder returns, balancing M&A like PixelForge for convergence.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee: What are your strategies for navigating the changing regulatory landscape?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Sarah. We're proactive: FCC Title II risks mitigated by advocacy and efficiencies; EU gigabit mandates via Vodafone JV; BEAD/RDOF for $42B subsidies. Spectrum: $500M in sensing for C-band. EU DSA/Ofcom via localized compliance. Overall, software-defined nets and convergence position us resiliently.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our performance this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainability. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
